title: How to compare commercial furniture suppliers in Australia
excerpt: A practical supplier comparison covering brief, product evidence, lead times, installation, warranties and whole-of-project responsibility.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Compare Commercial Furniture Suppliers | Your Office Space
metaDescription: Compare commercial furniture suppliers using product evidence, lead times, installation scope, warranties and whole-of-project responsibility.
body:
## Start with the brief, not the catalogue

A supplier can only price and plan the right furniture when the workplace brief is clear. Record team size, work patterns, room types, accessibility needs, technology, existing items, delivery constraints and the operational date.

## Compare like with like

Ask each supplier to identify the manufacturer, model, dimensions, finish, warranty, certification, lead time, quantity, unit price, delivery and installation scope. A lower total is not comparable if it excludes the work or evidence another proposal includes.

## Test the product evidence

Confirm what supports claims about ergonomics, durability, materials, sustainability, fire performance and warranty. A sample or showroom visit can help, but it does not replace written specifications and terms.

## Clarify delivery responsibility

Record who measures the site, confirms access, coordinates building requirements, receives goods, installs, removes packaging, manages defects and signs off completion. Identify long-lead and substituted items before an order is approved.

## Check change control

The quote should state how changes, substitutions, damaged goods, delays and variations are handled. No supplier should change an approved product or finish without documented agreement.

## Make the decision visible

Use a comparison table with the same headings for every supplier. Separate verified facts from assumptions and unresolved questions. Then select against the needs of the workplace, not a single headline price.

Your Office Space can help prepare and compare a furniture brief where the project fits our current capability and delivery area. Product availability, pricing and lead times must be confirmed for the actual order.
